subject.title: Telegram DM direct.tools appears accepted by config but is not reliably enforced as per-user tool policy

question: Should Telegram `direct.*.tools` and `toolsBySender` remain a supported tool-permission boundary that must be enforced for DM runs, or should the accepted config surface be retired/diagnosed as unsupported?
rationale: The schema and types currently imply an enforced security boundary, but implementing it affects shared tool-policy precedence and channel ownership; automation should not choose that boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Enforce Direct Policy
options.body: Treat the existing config as intended and implement direct/DM-aware tool-policy resolution with account, wildcard, sender, and topic precedence tests plus live Telegram proof.

options.title: Retire Or Warn
options.body: If per-DM tool policy is not intended, remove or doctor-warn the config surface and update docs so operators do not rely on a false deny boundary.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Binding Policy
options.body: Defer this Telegram-specific surface until the broader per-binding policy design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/49567 defines one canonical precedence model.

recommendation.title: Enforce Direct Policy
recommendation.body: Treat the existing config as intended and implement direct/DM-aware tool-policy resolution with account, wildcard, sender, and topic precedence tests plus live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent shared policy and security-boundary history on the resolver path this issue needs to change.
